Name: Glotrot
Condition: you talk to anyone (pick a dialogue option, or speak to a shopkeeper)
What it is there: An illness caught from black ooze on odd strata. Your tongue rots away and you can no longer speak.
Why it fits: A curse here is a thing you must not do for a while. Not speaking is a clean one to carry into any game, since most have someone to talk to.

Name: Ironshank
Condition: you use a movement ability (a dash, dodge, roll, sprint or teleport)
What it is there: An illness caught from black ooze on even strata. The leg bones calcify, slowing movement badly (up to -80 move speed) in exchange for armour.
Why it fits: Glotrot's twin, from the same ooze, and the stiff legs translate directly: no fast movement while it lasts. Paired with Glotrot it makes a two-curse set from one source.

Name: Terrified
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game while running from X fights you could have taken, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it flees: it can't be fought for X turns"
Combat: Cannot attack; moves away from you
What it is there: A mental effect: the creature drops what it was doing and runs from the source until it wears off.
Why it fits: Fleeing is a goal any game can host (most let you avoid a fight), and on the board it is the first status that moves a body AWAY rather than hurting it.
Needs: new: a body that moves away

Name: Lovesick
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game while taking the first item or upgrade you are offered X times, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it won't attack you while it is Lovesick"
Combat: Does not attack you; follows you around the board
What it is there: Falling in love with the first thing you look at (an apple farmer's daughter, or a love injector). On an NPC it acts as a temporary charm: it follows whoever it fell for.
Why it fits: 'Love the first thing you see' becomes 'take the first thing you're offered', a goal any game with choices can host. On an enemy it is a charm, which the board has none of yet. It pairs with the Love Injector candidate.
Needs: new: a charmed body

Name: Hallucination
On Player: Your goals read garbled: each shows as a random other goal until you finish a game
On Enemy: Gains "it shows as a random other enemy"
Combat: Shown as a random enemy; its real goal is hidden until it is defeated
What it is there: Monsters and objects show as random other things, with silly messages, until it wears off.
Why it fits: NetHack's most memorable status. On the board it is a disguise, which nothing here does yet.
Needs: new: disguising what the board shows

Name: Blind
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without looking at its map, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it attacks a random lane"
Combat: Attacks a random lane instead of the nearest target
What it is there: You can't see; monsters you haven't sensed are invisible to you. A whole conduct (Zen) is playing blind.
Why it fits: 'Don't use the map' is a goal almost any game with a map can host, and it's the Zen conduct in miniature.
Clones: Distracted (Soulstone Survivors): a stacking debuff that lowers the chance to hit, capped between 30% and 60%

Name: Hungry
Condition: you finish a game without eating anything
What it is there: Nutrition runs down every turn; Hungry, then Weak, then Fainting, then starving to death.
Why it fits: NetHack's food clock, as a curse: eat something in each game you play or pay for it. Most roguelikes have food or healing to eat.

Name: Mesmerised
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without retreating from a fight, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it can't move away from you"
Combat: Can't move backward; still attacks
What it is there: A siren's spell: you find the caster irresistible and can't move away from it, though you can still fight.
Why it fits: 'Don't retreat' is a goal any game can host, and on the board it pins a body in place for a Push.

Name: Corona
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without hiding or sneaking past anything, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it can't turn invisible"
Combat: Can't be invisible; takes 1 more damage from bombs
What it is there: A glowing aura: no invisibility, much worse stealth, and attackers hit you more easily.
Why it fits: A direct answer to the Invisibility ability, and 'no stealth' is a goal stealth games and roguelikes alike can host.

Name: Slow
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without using any speed boost, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it moves 1 tile less"
Combat: Moves 1 fewer tile per turn
What it is there: Every action takes 50% longer.
Why it fits: Speed is a live buff (Mewgenics); its opposite is missing.

Name: Magical Contamination
Condition: you use magic or a magic item 3 times in one game
What it is there: Miscasts and some magic build up contamination; too much and you start to glow and mutate.
Why it fits: A curse about overdoing it rather than not doing it: use magic, but sparingly.

Name: Black Death
Condition: an undead enemy damages you
What it is there: A plague zombie whose every hit permanently drains the hero's maximum life.
Why it fits: A curse that names an enemy tag (undead, 9 bodies), so it bites in some runs and not others. The drained-max-life fear is Diablo's own.

Name: Insanity
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game while having rested or slept, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and a shadow of it joins the board"
Combat: Its shadow is an extra 1-Health body that vanishes when it does
What it is there: Low Sanity summons shadow creatures that only the insane can see; sleeping and good food restore it.
Why it fits: Sanity is half of Don't Starve. Resting to recover is a goal most games can host, and a shadow copy on the board is a new kind of threat.
Needs: new: a shadow copy of a body

Name: Darkness
Condition: you spend time in total darkness
What it is there: Charlie, the Night Monster, attacks anyone standing in complete darkness.
Why it fits: 'Stay in the light' is a curse any game with dark areas can host, and the Miner Hat candidate answers it.

Name: Doomed
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game within X attempts, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it is defeated after X more turns"
Combat: Counts down 1 each turn; defeated at 0
What it is there: A countdown: one stack falls off each turn, and the unit goes down when it reaches 0.
Why it fits: A timer on a goal fits the attempt tracker (spec §3.2); on a body it is the Fading ability as a status anyone can inflict.

Name: Soul Link
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game in which two enemies died to the same blow, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and damage to it is shared with every other Soul Linked body"
Combat: Damage to one linked body hits all of them; one bomb can clear the link
What it is there: A keyword: whenever a linked character loses health, every linked character loses it too.
Why it fits: Turns one bomb into several, which gives the board's bombs a new reason to be aimed.
Needs: new: bodies that share damage

Name: Tarred
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without using fire, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it moves X tiles less"
Combat: Moves X tiles less; Fire turns all its Tarred into Burn
What it is there: Slows by a step per stack; any Fire turns every stack of Tarred into Burn.
Why it fits: A status that combos with the two fire pieces the board has (the Fire tile and Burn): slow them, then light them.

Name: Madness
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game in which an enemy hurt another enemy, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it attacks the nearest body, friend or foe"
Combat: Attacks the nearest body, including other enemies
What it is there: The unit sees everything as an enemy and is AI-controlled until it wears off.
Why it fits: Turns the stack against itself; the Ruthless ability already lets a body hit its own side.

Name: Midas Touch
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game while carrying more gold than you started it with, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it drops 1 Gold when defeated, however it dies"
Combat: Turned to gold: can't move or attack for 1 turn; drops 1 Gold when defeated (even by a bomb)
What it is there: From the Midas' Touch item: enemies that touch Isaac are turned to gold and drop pennies when killed.
Why it fits: A bombed body pays nothing today (spec §14.1); this is the one status that would make it pay.
Builds on: gold per enemy, bombs, Golden Idol

Name: Curse of the Blind
Condition: you use an unidentified loot
What it is there: A floor curse: every item is shown as a question mark until it's picked up.
Why it fits: This game's version of not knowing what you pick up is the identify gamble (scrolls, potions, wands, pills); the curse taxes gambling on it.

Name: Stress
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without losing a fight in it, or take 3 Damage." At 10 Stress it becomes a random Debuff, or (1 in 4) a random Buff
On Enemy: Gains "and it is easier to rattle: its goal ticks at any time"
Combat: Stacks; at 10 the body breaks: it skips its turn
What it is there: Heroes build up stress from fights, crits and horrors; at 100 they face an Affliction (most of the time) or a Virtue.
Why it fits: Darkest Dungeon's defining system. A meter that tips into a random Debuff or, rarely, a Buff is the Affliction/Virtue roll the random-status verbs can already make.
Needs: new: a status that converts at a threshold

Name: Blight
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without being poisoned, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it takes 1 damage at the start of each of its turns"
Combat: Takes 1 damage at the start of its turn for X turns
What it is there: Darkest Dungeon's poison: damage over time, resisted by Blight resistance.
Why it fits: Damage over time is missing from the statuses here (Burn halves damage dealt instead), and the Gas Cloud tile candidate needs a poison to apply.
Needs: new: damage over time

Name: Cave Adaptation
Condition: you go outside into daylight
What it is there: Dwarves who stay underground too long grow sick in sunlight: irritated, or nauseated and vomiting.
Why it fits: A curse to stay underground, the reverse of Darkness (stay in the light). Most dungeon games have an outside.

Name: Wet
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without using fire, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it loses Fireproof and any Buff"
Combat: Loses Fireproof and its Buffs; can't Burn while Wet
What it is there: Wet makes a body lose its protections, which no status does yet; it also answers the Fire tile.
Why it fits: A status effect: the character loses existing immunities and some buffs, and it negates effects like Fleeing and Burning.
Builds on: Fireproof ability, Burn, Fire tile, Phial of Floods (candidate)

Name: Teleportitis
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game after being moved somewhere you didn't choose, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it teleports to a random square each turn"
Combat: Teleports to a random empty square at the start of its turn
What it is there: A body that won't stay put scrambles the board's lanes, which nothing does each turn yet.
Why it fits: A status from Teleportatium and some enemies: the stained creature teleports at random.

Name: Blood Pact
Condition: you use a bomb or any explosive
What it is there: Costs health to plant a bomb; Sweaty Palms with it is a death spiral.
Why it fits: Bombs are a verb here and in most action roguelikes, so 'don't use them' is a real ask.

Name: Mediocrity
Condition: you land a critical hit
What it is there: Sets critical strike chance to 0, making every crit relic useless.
Why it fits: Critical hits are in most games with numbers; it's a clean thing to forbid for a few games.

Name: Tariffs
Condition: you buy anything
What it is there: Everything costs 1.5 times as much: gold, health, keys and curses.
Why it fits: A curse on shopping: buy nothing for a while or pay for it.

Name: Compulsion
Condition: you finish a game still holding a potion or consumable you picked up in it
What it is there: Every potion is drunk the moment it's picked up. "They say 'a healthy life is one of moderation,' but they also say 'you only live once.'"
Why it fits: The other side of hoarding: use what you find straight away.

Name: Discorded
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game while having made two enemies fight each other, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it attacks the enemies next to it instead of you"
Combat: Attacks its neighbours; they attack it back
What it is there: A monster that attacks, and is attacked by, its own allies; it will still attack you if you're its closest enemy.
Why it fits: The board has charm (Lovesick, candidate) but nothing that turns bodies on each other; on the player it becomes a goal about doing exactly that.
Builds on: statuses' goal modes, Staff of Discord (candidate)
Needs: new: enemies attacking enemies

Name: Cursed
Condition: you take any damage before you have defeated 10 enemies
What it is there: Dead Cells' curse: any damage at all kills you outright until you have killed enough enemies to lift it. Cursed chests, doors and the Cursed Sword give it, and it pays (scrolls, gems, healing).
Why it fits: The hardest curse to carry and the cleanest to explain: don't get hit. It lifts by fighting, not by waiting.
Needs: new: a curse that lifts after defeated enemies, not games

Name: Petrify
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without using your strongest weapon or ability, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and you can't use your strongest weapon or ability while doing it"
Combat: Its ability does nothing for X turns
What it is there: A keyword: turns sides of the target's die into petrified blanks, one side per pip, in a fixed order.
Why it fits: Stun skips a whole turn; Petrify blanks part of what a body can do, which is the dice game's own kind of debuff.
Needs: new: switching off a body's ability for a while

Name: Jammed
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without picking up a cursed item, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Jammed: beat it and Gain a [chest reward]"
Combat: Deals double damage
What it is there: The curse's enemy modifier: Jammed enemies glow crimson in black smoke, deal a full heart (twice the damage), move and shoot 50% faster, and drop more. More Curse, more of them; at 10 the Lord of the Jammed hunts you.
Why it fits: A status that makes a body worse and better at once: deadlier, and worth more. The board's statuses are all one or the other.
Needs: new: a status that raises a body's payout

Name: Frog
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without attacking anything for its first minute, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it's a frog while you do it: it can't fight back"
Combat: Can't attack; takes double damage
What it is there: Koh or a monster that steps on a Frog trap or eats a Tumna fruit becomes a Lazy Frog: it can't attack, its shield doesn't work and it takes more damage, until the effect wears off.
Why it fits: Polymorph that leaves the body on the board, harmless and fragile: Noita's Polymorphine (candidate) is a potion that does it once, this is the status it leaves.
Needs: new: a status that stops attacks and doubles damage taken

Name: Hangover
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without drinking anything, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and you can't drink a potion while doing it"
Combat: Deals 1 less damage
What it is there: What Drunk leaves behind half the time: -10% to everything for a day.
Why it fits: 'Get drunk' is a live goal; this is the morning after, and it pairs with it.

Name: Color Blind
Condition: you play a game in colour (turn on greyscale to avoid it)
What it is there: A Rogue Legacy trait: 'You can't see colors.' Every heir has 0-2 random traits, and this one turns the whole game greyscale.
Why it fits: Rogue Legacy's traits are handicaps for one life; this one carries straight into any game (turn greyscale on).

Name: Normality
Condition: you use more than 3 items or abilities in one fight
What it is there: A curse card: 'You cannot play more than 3 cards this turn.'
Why it fits: A curse on doing too much: a cap on actions, which translates to any game with abilities and items.

Name: Riposte
On Player: Gain "If you parry or counter X attacks when beating a game, Gain a [chest reward]"
On Enemy: Gains "and you must parry or counter an attack in the run you complete the goal in"
Combat: When bashed, it hits back for 1
What it is there: Counter-attacks the next damaging attack it receives; lasts 3 turns, up to 3.
Why it fits: DD2's counter token, and the Highwayman's signature. DCSS's level-up 'countered an attack' (candidate) is the same act as a level-up.
Needs: new: retaliation

Name: Stealth
On Player: Gain "If you get past X enemies without being seen when beating a game, Gain a [chest reward]"
On Enemy: Gains "and you must get past an enemy unseen in the run you complete the goal in"
Combat: Weapons can't target it while another body stands; it loses Stealth when it attacks
What it is there: A unit with Stealth can't be targeted while an ally without it can be; attacking removes it.
Why it fits: The Runaway's and the Highwayman's token, and the reason a hero hides in the back rank.
Builds on: The King is Watching's 'Sneak past a sleeping enemy' goal (candidate)
Needs: new: untargetable

Name: Curse of Haphephobia
Condition: you touch a wall
What it is there: One of the seven cursed weapon keywords: 'Touching walls hurts'. A cursed weapon gives 2 HP and +5% damage, then binds itself to you until it breaks or is blessed.
Why it fits: A curse you can play around in any game with walls, and it says so in one line.

Name: Scared
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without running from a fight, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and you must make an enemy flee in the run you complete the goal in"
Combat: On its turn it moves back a column instead of attacking
What it is there: A scared creature tries to flee on its next turn, and hides if it can't.
Why it fits: Fleeing is half of FtK's combat (a Fleeing status of its own); this is what makes a body back off.

Name: Foolish
Condition: you look up a guide or a wiki while playing
What it is there: One of FtK2's seven curses, each a stat at -25 that only Hag's Bane or a town Priest removes; Foolish takes Intelligence.
Why it fits: A curse on knowing things is a natural one for a game played on the honour system.

Name: Tension
Game: Dragon Quest: Young Yangus and the Mystery Dungeon
On Player: Gain "If you charge up an attack X times when beating a game, Gain a [chest reward]"
On Enemy: Gains "and you must charge up an attack in the run you complete the goal in"
Combat: It does not move this turn; its next hit does +X damage
What it is there: Dragon Quest's charge-up: the game's own overview lists the Tension command as new to the series here, building attack power for a strong blow while the character cannot move.
Why it fits: Psyche Up and Tension are Dragon Quest's signature; For the King 2's Fallen Knight (a candidate today) has a level-up built on the same act, and this is the better-known home for it.
Needs: new: a status that holds a body still

Name: Burnout
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game within X attempts, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it burns out: after X turns it is defeated by itself, and the goal with it"
Combat: Counts down 1 each turn; at 0 the body is defeated
What it is there: A countdown: it ticks down every turn, and when it runs out the unit dies. The Melting Remnant's wax units carry it.
Why it fits: A body that will go out on its own is a different kind of threat on the board: wait it out or deal with it now.
Builds on: For the King's countdown goal (The Hangman, candidate)
Needs: new: a body defeated by a timer

Name: Bear Transform
Combat: Enemy only. Counts down 1 each turn; at 0 the body becomes a Bear: +1 Health and +1 Damage
What it is there: A counter that drops by one every turn; when it reaches zero, the unit turns into a bear.
Why it fits: A body with a fuse: deal with it now or face the bear. Nothing else on the board changes what it is mid-fight.
Needs: new: a body that becomes another enemy on a timer

Name: Shrunk
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without dealing a full hit (half damage only), or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Shrunk: anything that walks into it crushes it"
Combat: Deals half damage. An enemy that moves or is pushed into it crushes it: it is defeated
What it is there: The character becomes tiny and deals 66% less damage; any other character who touches them while moving crushes them, instantly. Crushing a shrunk person isn't treated as an attack.
Why it fits: A body that is weak but dies to a push, which makes Push and Bash do something new together.
Needs: new: a body defeated by being walked into

Name: Guilt
Condition: you run away from a fight (leave an area while an enemy there is still alive)
What it is there: 'To run away from danger like so does not fit the way of the Templars.' A curse for fleeing; Frightened, its twin, comes from leaving a room with an enemy nearby.
Why it fits: A soldier's shame, as a rule any game can host: no running from a fight.

Name: Overdose
Condition: you use 3 or more healing items in one game
What it is there: 'Consuming all of these concoctions made me sick.' Given for using 5 needles in a life; Anesthesia and Habitual phenomenon are the same curse for poultices.
Why it fits: Most games have a healing item, and a limit on chugging them is a real constraint. Normality (a candidate) caps every item and ability in a fight; this caps only healing, across a whole game. Hungry (a candidate) is the opposite rule.
Clones: Oversaturated (Barony): eating too much food makes you vomit, the same rule for food rather than healing items

Name: Manipulated
Condition: you switch weapons
What it is there: 'A dark voice tells you it loves you and wants to remain with you forever.' The Jealous Hatchet's curse: you cannot change weapon sets.
Why it fits: A clean rule for any game with more than one weapon. It is also what the Jealous Hatchet (a candidate) gives you.

Name: Glass Bones
Condition: you take damage from a fall
What it is there: 'I shouldn't jump from so high carrying such heavy equipment.' After one bad fall, falling far enough to be winded again deals 5 damage.
Why it fits: Platformers and action games are full of drops; this makes every ledge a decision.

Name: Pox
Combat: Enemy only. Stacks. When it reaches 3 stacks the body takes 3 damage and the stacks clear
What it is there: 'On 3 Pox: Deal 10 Damage and remove 3 stacks of Pox.' A hit that would go past 3 starts a new set.
Why it fits: A fuse you build up yourself, three hits at a time; Burn and Bleed tick, this bursts.

Name: Pyromaniac
On Player: Gain "You must start a fire in this game, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it is a Pyromaniac: it sets fires"
Combat: At the end of its turn, 1 in 2 it sets its own square on Fire
What it is there: A mental ailment: the companion has a 50% chance to start fires after exploring a shrine or cave, eating a mushroom, or resting in the open.
Why it fits: A body that spreads the Fire tile around itself, which can hurt the enemies beside it as much as you.

Name: Claustrophobic
Condition: you go into a cave, a tunnel or anywhere underground
What it is there: A mental ailment: the companion panics in caves, loses loyalty exploring one in the dark, and is doomed if sent into a narrow crevice.
Why it fits: A clean rule for any game with a below: stay above ground. Cave Adaptation (a candidate) is the opposite rule.

Name: Acrophobia
Condition: you climb to a high place (a mountain, a tower, a rooftop)
What it is there: A mental ailment: the companion loses loyalty whenever the trek climbs or travels on hills or plateaus; resting at Healing Springs can give it.
Why it fits: Keeps you low for three games. Glass Bones (a candidate) is about falling; this is about going up at all.

Name: Superstitious
Condition: you use a shrine, an altar, a statue or a tomb
What it is there: A mental ailment: the companion loses Loyalty, and may turn Angry, whenever the player interacts with Stone Circles, Tombs, Shrines or Stone Statues.
Why it fits: Most games have something holy to touch; this curse makes you walk past it. It also keeps you off the candidate altars and wells.

Name: Brittle
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without being hit more than 3 times, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Brittle: every hit lands harder"
Combat: Stacks. Every hit on it Stuns 1 more for each stack
What it is there: A debuff: each stack adds 1 damage to every incoming damage instance, direct hits and damage-over-time alike, for 5 seconds.
Why it fits: The live Marked doubles one hit; Brittle adds a little to every hit, so it rewards many small weapons over one big one.

Name: Crippled
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game while taking damage every time you run or dash, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Crippled: moving hurts it"
Combat: Stacks. Each time it moves (or is pushed), it takes 1 damage per stack; 1 stack wears off each turn
What it is there: 'Whenever this character moves, they take damage equal to stacks of Crippled.' Ticks down by 1 at the end of the character's turn.
Why it fits: Every body on the board walks toward you, so moving costing Health makes Push and Dash weapons twice as good.

Name: Protected
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Protected: the body in front takes its hits"
Combat: Enemy only. Hits on it go to the body directly in front of it instead, until that body falls or it stops standing behind one
What it is there: 'Whenever this character receives damage, up to 25 damage is redirected to the ally directly in front.' It ends when the protector dies or the character is no longer behind them.
Why it fits: The board is front-to-back, and a bodyguard in front of a dangerous back-line body asks you to clear the line in order, or Push around it.
Needs: new: damage passed to another body

Name: Leeching
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Leeching: it heals the bodies around it"
Combat: Enemy only. At the start of its turn, every other body next to it heals 1. When it deals damage, it heals 1
What it is there: An elite type: Leeching elites passively heal nearby enemies and regenerate health when they deal damage (all elites have 2.8x health and drop double gold).
Why it fits: A body worth killing first, which changes the order you clear the board in. Bombs and row weapons get better against a cluster around it.
Needs: new: healing between enemy bodies

Name: Suit Malfunction
Condition: you stand still while an enemy is near
What it is there: Malignant items and Parasites cause Malfunctions, each a penalty with a task beside it that removes it (kill hostiles, open containers, use keys). One reads 'While stationary, -75% Weapon Damage'.
Why it fits: Keep moving is a rule any action game can host. Returnal's twist is the removal task, which would let a curse be lifted by play instead of waited out.
Needs: new (optional): a curse lifted by a task (defeat 3 enemies, open a chest, use a Key) instead of a timer
Clones: Oklob Plant (Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup): a goal asking the opposite, to win a fight without moving

Name: Quasimorphosis
Condition: you eat meat or flesh
What it is there: A meter that rises with time and every death on the floor, and greatly when you eat meat (human, dog or spider flesh); past a point quasimorphs step into reality, and at 1000 a Baron arrives. Luxury food, spirits and drugs lower it.
Why it fits: spawn_enemy is exactly its penalty: what you eat calls the monsters. Most games with food have meat in them, so the rule is real. Hungry (a candidate) is the opposite ask, to eat at all.

Name: Electrify
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Electrified: when it is hit, the bodies around it are hit too"
Combat: Enemy only. Whenever it takes damage, every other body next to it takes 1
What it is there: A status effect: electrified enemies damage surrounding enemies when taking damage.
Why it fits: A status that rewards packed boards and single-target weapons alike. Soul Link (a candidate) passes damage to linked bodies anywhere; this passes it to neighbours.

Name: Blood Lust
Condition: you take more than a minute to defeat one enemy
What it is there: Curse 30: lose HP if you don't defeat enemies quickly enough. Curses come from cursed relics, Curse Chests and some relic effects, and each makes corrupted enemies likelier.
Why it fits: A clock on every fight, which any game with enemies can host. Most curse candidates forbid an action; this one demands speed.

Name: Hungry Locks
Condition: you open a lock or a locked door with a key
What it is there: Curse 3: a chance of losing an additional key upon using one.
Why it fits: Locks are in nearly every dungeon game, and this makes every one a choice for a while. It also bites the key candidates (Key Master, Flynt, Lock-a-doora).

Name: Tasty
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Tasty: defeating it feeds you"
Combat: Enemy only. When it is defeated, you gain +1 Max Health
What it is there: An ailment: when a pet with it is defeated, the opposite team gets a permanent +2 attack and +2 health. The Sea Cucumber gives it to random enemies at the start of battle.
Why it fits: A target worth taking first, and a reason to apply a status to the strongest body. No status here pays you for a kill yet.

Name: Dread
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game while having done something that made you happy in it, or take 3 Damage."
Combat: Stacks. At 3 stacks the body breaks: it is defeated at the end of its next turn unless a stack is removed first
What it is there: 'Despair, the wolf that devours thought.' An ill-health card: Bleak Thoughts gathers Dread, and three of it start a countdown to the No More ending unless Contentment is found in time. Its opposite is Fascination.
Why it fits: A status cured by joy rather than by medicine: the goal asks you to do something you enjoy (a song, a meal, a win) in whatever you're playing.

Name: Tranquility
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Tranquil: it hits harder until it moves"
Combat: It deals +1 damage until it moves or is pushed; then Tranquility ends
What it is there: A buff: deal 30% more damage, which wears off if you move too far.
Why it fits: A body worth moving: Push and the swap weapons break it. The Tension candidate charges a hit by standing still once; this lasts until it moves.

Name: Black Retribution
Condition: you land the killing blow on an enemy
What it is there: An unplayable curse card: it deals 5 damage to you whenever you kill an enemy while it is in your hand.
Why it fits: A curse on killing itself, which turns a game toward allies, traps and the environment doing the work. The Ambas Worm candidate's goal asks who lands the blow; this forbids you to.

Name: Fool's Bounty
Condition: you open a chest
What it is there: A general curse: opening a gold chest now inflicts Corruption, but gold chests contain more gold. Corruption fills by doors and blood offerings; every full gauge brings a curse, and a fifth is final.
Why it fits: Chests are in nearly every game, and this makes each one a question. Tariffs (a candidate) curses buying; this curses looting.

Name: Allergy
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without healing in it, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Allergic: healing hurts it"
Combat: Healing it would get instead deals that much damage to it
What it is there: A status effect: units become allergic to heals, taking damage from healing effects, vampirism included.
Why it fits: Turns the healer enemies (the Priestess, the Proteron, Leeching) against their own side. The live The Head asks the same of the player as a goal; here it rides a status.

Name: Glaciate
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Glaciated: frozen solid, and shatters if pushed into the edge"
Combat: It can't move or attack for 1 turn. Pushed into the edge of the board or another body while Glaciated, it is defeated outright
What it is there: A status from the Omenforged's Glaciating Frost: the enemy can't move or attack for 2.5 seconds, and launching it into a wall kills it instantly. One stack at a time.
Why it fits: A freeze with a finisher, so it pairs a Stun with Push: the Mountie Hockey Stick and the push pieces become executions.
Needs: new: defeat on a push into the edge

Name: Buffer
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Buffered: the next status put on it is shrugged off"
Combat: The next status applied to it is blocked, and Buffer ends
What it is there: A buff: each stack prevents one harmful debuff; if a target is about to be burned, one stack is consumed and none of the burn lands.
Why it fits: A ward against the status pieces that makes you spend a cheap one first. No status here guards against statuses yet.

Name: Exposed
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Exposed: one blow finishes it"
Combat: The next hit defeats it outright (bosses excepted), and you Gain +1 Shield
What it is there: A status: an Exposed foe can be destroyed with a Takedown, which makes it explode and drop Shield Pickups.
Why it fits: A finisher window as a status, the way Doom's glory kills pay you for the kill. The Executioner candidate's goal asks for one; this makes one.

Name: Educated
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Educated: its blows heal you instead"
Combat: Damage it would deal you heals you instead, until the game ends
What it is there: A status condition: the card's total power is multiplied by -1, shown by a blue graduation cap. It comes from accepting the Education Opportunity, from Magister Miksha, or from the fight with Archdean Hergel.
Why it fits: A joke about schooling that turns a threat into a help, with the strongest body the best one to Educate.
Needs: new: damage turned into healing

Name: Meditate
On Player: Gain "If you win a fight without moving X times when beating a game, Gain a [chest reward]"
Combat: Deals +1 Damage for each turn it has stood still
What it is there: An effect: +10 damage dealt per stack, and half the stacks are lost on every step. Monks and stillness powers build it.
Why it fits: The reward form of standing still, which the curses only punish (Returnal's Suit Malfunction).
Clones: Oklob Plant (Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup): the goal 'Win a fight without moving' carried by an enemy rather than a status

Name: Last Will
Combat: When this body is defeated, 1 in 2 it drops a random Potion
What it is there: A common Curse spell: a unit that dies while carrying Last Will has a chance to drop a random potion (Healing, Mana or Stamina). It can be cast on enemies, allies and other Spellmasons.
Why it fits: A debuff that pays you when its body falls, so it changes which enemy you go for first; nothing on the board drops loot yet.

Name: Avarice
On Player: Gain "You must spend X Gold before you finish a game, or lose all your Gold."
What it is there: A Tribulation: at the start of the run the Burden of Avarice is placed on the board; feed it 10, 25 or 50 balls (Easy, Normal, Hard) by the last drop, or lose all your money.
Why it fits: A debt with a deadline: hoarding is punished all at once instead of a little at a time, and the shop becomes a place you must go.
Clones: Coin Bomb (Neon Abyss): unspent gold explodes after one game, for 1 Damage, a trinket rather than a status

Name: Confused
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game with two of your controls swapped, or take 3 Damage."
Combat: Moves to a random square next to it instead of forward; it still attacks if you're in reach
What it is there: From a potion of confusion (or a scroll of monster confusion, which makes your next hit confuse a monster): you stagger in random directions for a while.
Why it fits: Hallucination and Blind (NetHack) are candidates, and confusion is the third of the classic trio; swapping controls is possible in almost any game with key rebinding.
Needs: new: random movement on the board

Name: Lunarity
On Player: Gain "If you beat a game at night (by your own clock), Gain a [chest reward]"
Combat: Deals double damage for 2 turns, then half damage for 2 turns, and so on
What it is there: The moon's phase shown at the side of the screen: when it matches your alignment you hit far more often and deal double damage; when it opposes it, you deal half.
Why it fits: A status that swings, where every other status is steady; the chest-reward goal ties it to the real night, the way Omega's ties it to the game's moon.
Needs: new: an effect that swings between turns

Name: Overeating
Condition: you eat or drink something to heal while already at full health
What it is there: Food heals you slowly, and too little starves you; but eating too much makes you sluggish, and a full food meter kills you outright from overeating.
Why it fits: A curse about a habit the player has in any game (topping up for no reason), and the opposite end of NetHack's Hungry.
Clones: Hungry (NetHack): the other end of the stomach, for finishing a game without eating

Name: Overburn
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Overburned: once its Overburn passes its Health, it explodes"
Combat: Does nothing while it stacks. The moment an enemy's Overburn is greater than its Health it is defeated, dealing damage equal to its Overburn to every enemy in its row
What it is there: A Shademancer debuff: no effect until the card has more Overburn than health, then it explodes, dealing its Overburn to itself and every ally in its row.
Why it fits: A debuff that is a fuse rather than a drain: nothing happens until the count crosses the target's health, then the whole row pays.
Needs: new: a status that triggers on crossing Health

Name: Ink
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without using a special ability, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Inked: its ability is crossed out"
Combat: Its ability does nothing; it still moves and attacks. Counts down 1 each turn
What it is there: A Clunkmaster debuff that crosses out all of a card's ability text, though it still counts down and attacks; it wears off by 1 a turn.
Why it fits: Silence as a status: the board's abilities (§7.6) have nothing that switches one off yet.
Needs: new: suppressing an ability

Name: Night
Game: Shiren the Wanderer 4: The Eye of God and the Devil's Navel
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game defeating enemies only with abilities or items, never a plain attack, or take 3 Damage."
Combat: Player only. Your weapons deal 1 damage. Enemies deal +1 damage. Every enemy defeated while it lasts drops an extra reward
What it is there: Day and Night, new in Shiren 4: at night Night Monsters spawn, nearly every attack is turned into 1 damage so you need Techniques or staves, some monsters attack each other, you can't read scrolls without a torch, and night monsters hit harder but every item they drop is blessed.
Why it fits: A status that turns the plain attack off and pays for it: high risk, better drops.
Needs: new: capping weapon damage

Name: Ether Disease
On Player: Gain "After each game, 1 in 3: gain a random symptom that stays for the run. Some symptoms are pure drawbacks, some trade a drawback for a perk."
Combat: Player only. Symptoms stack; the same one can come twice
What it is there: A series of random corruptions received over time, like mutations, except each symptom is either wholly negative or both positive and negative; the Etherwind and ether equipment speed it up, some cloaks and the Elea race slow it.
Why it fits: A status that never ends and keeps adding: the run's own clock as a disease.
Needs: new: a pool of lasting symptoms

Name: Unidentified Illness
On Player: Gain "You carry one of four hidden illnesses. It shows only as Unidentified Illness until something identifies it."
On Enemy: Gains "and it carries a hidden illness, named only once it is defeated"
Combat: A random hidden Debuff; its name is shown only when identified or when the body is defeated
What it is there: Four parasites (tapeworm, bloodworms, brainworms, paincysts) all display as 'Unidentified Illness: You aren't sure what's wrong with you but you don't feel well', each doing something different underneath; a blood draw and analysis tells you which.
Why it fits: Unidentified loot's guessing game, applied to a status.
Needs: new: a hidden status

Name: Hoarder
On Player: Gain "At the start of each game, take 1 Damage if 3 or more cells of your pack are empty."
Combat: Player only. Any piece fills its cells, junk included
What it is there: A mutation: 'You don't feel right unless you're carrying a bunch of stuff. You want to always have the right tool for every occasion... even carrying junk helps keep the horrible thoughts quiet.'
Why it fits: It pushes against an empty pack in a game where pack shape is the loot system.
Clones: Mouse Wood (Backpack Hero): rewards empty cells instead

Name: Restless
Condition: you go back to a place in the game you have already been
What it is there: The end of a mutation chain (Nomad, Antsy, Restless): 'Spending any amount of time in familiar places makes you miserable. Must. Keep. Moving.'
Why it fits: A plain thing to forbid that almost any game can test.

Name: Brawler
Condition: you use a ranged weapon or attack (a gun, a bow, a thrown weapon or a projectile spell)
What it is there: A trait: 'using ranged weapons is off-limits to you, even if your life depended on it'; its softer sibling Gun-Shy forbids only firearms.
Why it fits: A plain thing to forbid that almost any game can test.

Name: Illiterate
Condition: you read anything in the game: a book, a note, a sign, a terminal or a lore entry
What it is there: A starting trait: 'You never learned to read! Books and computers are off-limits to you.'
Why it fits: A plain thing to forbid that almost any game can test.

Name: Sub-Healthy
Condition: you are poisoned, fall ill or catch a disease in the game
What it is there: A negative soldier trait. It once made soldiers die suddenly; since the AG-27 directive it 'increases the chance of becoming ill instead'.
Why it fits: Poison and sickness are in a great many games, so the condition comes up without being forced.

Name: Pain Reversal
On Player: Gain "The next time you would take Damage, gain that much Health instead."
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Reversed: the next hit on it heals it"
Combat: The next damage this body takes heals it instead; then it wears off
What it is there: A beneficial Body status from the skill of the same name: 'A portion of the next damage taken heals instead.' It is removed the moment its holder is damaged.
Why it fits: A one-hit ward that turns a blow into healing, readable in a line, and as useful to an enemy body as to you.

Name: Rot
On Player: Gain "If you lose a game while Rotting, lose 1 Max Health as well as Health. Healing or Burn cures it."
On Enemy: Gains "and it is Rotting: it loses Health each turn, a little more every turn"
Combat: Takes 1 Damage at the start of its turn, 1 more each turn after. Healing it or Burning it removes Rot
What it is there: A harmful Body status: 'Inflicts escalating damage over time and may permanently lower maximum HP. Has a chance to be cured when healed or hit by fire damage.' It cannot be dispelled.
Why it fits: Damage over time that grows, with a cure the game already has (Burn, healing), so it reads against Fire tiles and potions.

Name: Curse of Vanishing
Condition: you leave a pickup (a coin, a heart, ammo) on the floor and move on without it
What it is there: One of five curses that come with a cut-price shop item: 'Pickups disappear faster. Pickups, including hearts, coins and pills, disappear faster.'
Why it fits: Almost every game drops pickups, so the condition comes up, and it turns a habit (leaving the small change) into a risk.

Name: Broken Leg
On Player: Gain "You must beat a game without running or dodge-rolling, or take 3 Damage."
On Enemy: Gains "and it has a Broken Leg: it moves 1 square at most"
Combat: Speed -1, and it cannot move more than 1 square a turn
What it is there: A wound from the arena: 'Each day in the arena leaves you with new wounds to add to your misery.' Coverage lists 'a broken leg, a missing eye, and paranoia-induced hallucinations' among dozens of conditions.
Why it fits: A lasting injury that rewrites how you play, testable in any game with a run or a dodge.

Name: Paranoia
On Player: Gain "You see enemies that are not there: the next board stands one false enemy among the real ones."
Combat: Player only. A false enemy stands on the board; it does nothing and vanishes when hit, and you cannot tell it from the rest until then
What it is there: Another arena wound: 'paranoia-induced hallucinations'.
Why it fits: A debuff that lies to you about the board rather than hurting you, which no live status does.
Needs: new: a false body on the board
